perspectives.summary: Automatic label unavailable; top terms: remake, oot, game.

representative_posts.author: hellagur.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: the interesting thing about the oot remake to me is that it doesn't necessarily make the core experience of playing through oot any different than if you played the original but it adds a lot more life and detail to the game's world than was present in the original

representative_posts.author: pizzafacts.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Almost finished with the oot remake and i really really like what they did with the climactic escape sequence. Zelda is cool

representative_posts.author: kenziekuma.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: being cell shaded b/c they wanted E rated combat w/enemies exploding into items, but didn't want to be too goofy for a realistic style, but I'd say the OoT remake totally nailed it! I hope the OoT Remake leads into a new game like how Link's Awakening lead to Echoes of Wisdom!

representative_posts.author: puckiedhole.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm gonna be fully honest, I was skeptical of the OoT remake before launch, but Nintendo has convinced me. I think this is not a remake born as a recession indicator, or Nintendo needing a cashgrab to sell Sw2. They have managed to take something that was magical back then and made it magical now.

representative_posts.author: wilburwurthless.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: the OoT remake is beautiful and a lot of fun but it’s making me want to do a playthrough of TotK next. I miss that open world freedom

representative_posts.author: hellagur.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: it feels so simple but i don't think i've seen this approach with a lot of remakes. the stuff they added isn't as much in the gameplay or the story as it is fleshing out the world and the people who live in it

representative_posts.author: cartridgegames.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Remake first, probably I guess you would appreciate the changes more if you played the old ones first but it’s a great game you can enjoy fully standalone

representative_posts.author: chopchopok.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I'm extremely impressed at how good the game feels to play. This is a game I thought about a lot during my childhood. I remember the whole story beat for beat, and most of the dungeon rooms as well. And yet the remake feels fresh to play. I keep wanting to play more.

representative_posts.author: rotto.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: For every one change I dislike there are about 5 things to compensate for it, so it ultimately isn't a big deal. Definitely not enough to write the remake off as a "bastardization" or slop

representative_posts.author: hylian.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I remember when the remake was announced I was bummed that it was 1:1. Mostly due to my experience with LA switch being pretty mid. But the OoT remake proved me wrong in every single way. Things I’d been waiting 30 yrs for happened in this remake. Massive lore inclusions too. Perfect forever game

representative_posts.text: remake, and that's good -- hopefully it starts to open up soon because I'm getting angry

perspectives.title: Whale Summon Book
perspectives.summary: Automatic label unavailable; top terms: whale, summon, book.

representative_posts.author: tpwrtrmnky.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If "summon whale" actually works like that, why isn't EVERYONE who knows Summon Whale deploying whale bombardments? Is it believable that the main character is the first one to have thought of that?

representative_posts.author: amaryllis-sera.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Well, exactly? This is all in favour of doing thoughtful and intentional worldbuilding and thinking what the bounds of your magic system are. Your answer here is "yes, actually we do need to have a specific answer on whether it's possible to summon the whale in mid-air (it's no, and implied)".

representative_posts.author: tpwrtrmnky.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My point is, if your version of "summon whale" needs that clarified in the first place, you're writing a video game ability rather than a magic power for a character in a story. Asking specific wildlife to help you and then getting that help is primarily a thematic thing, not a mechanical one.

representative_posts.author: capnbooker.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: This is maybe my favorite line in the book, in modern context. Because the point is that Moby Dick, the novel, is not an allegory. It's meant to recount the very real, very dangerous, and very easily exploitable circumstances of whaling.

representative_posts.author: latisserande.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: tbf I could see some types of less-than-serious fantasy fiction run with "summon a whale in mid-air, it crashes onto the ground, covering an entire enemy base in blood and gore"

representative_posts.author: ferrerman.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Alright then, so Moby Dick wasn't necessarily really about a whale then?

representative_posts.author: capnbooker.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The flattened interpretation that Moby Dick is an allegory about revenge misses so much of the point. It's the reason people bemoan the parts of the book that are "just facts about whaling." Because the whaling is the point. It's basically "The Jungle," but for sailors.

representative_posts.author: amaryllis-sera.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I want fiction with real feeling characters in real feeling worlds, not shallow puppets. If a (smart/scrappy) character has a "summon whale" spell, why *aren't* they thinking about how to use it effectively, what the bounds of it are etc. Are their problems not real to them?
